redditMentions.body: Current CE, just finished my second year. The other posts pretty much cover everything, but I just wanted to say that generally as a CE you can get most CS jobs, provided that you invest some of your own time to learn about more "core" CS topics like algorithms, data structures, and runtime analysis which are not covered until "Fundamentals of Algorithms" (formerly "Optimization Methods" -- excellent class, btw), and are still not covered as thoroughly as they are covered in CS classes. The opposite is not necessarily true; if you are in CS and are interested in a job closer to hardware is it my understanding that you won't have the background in circuits/electronics/digital logic for that (CS people, please do correct me if I'm wrong!). I was in the exact same situation as you two years ago. I wasn't sure which one to choose; I had programming experience and knew I liked programming, but **ultimately I chose CE because I was more interested in learning about how computers work at a practical level, rather than a theoretical level**. That said, CS classes do get very practical later on in the curriculum. At the beginning I was pretty fixed on solely programing and software engineering for my career but as I've taken more classes I've actually grown to enjoy hardware a lot more than I was expecting and find myself really attracted to embedded systems work (the border between hardware and software). A nice mix of both CE and CS. Either way, I highly encourage you to explore both majors in your first semester. Talk to different people in both and even professors to get a better sense of what you're looking for. For more information on CE I recommend shooting Professor David Kaeli an email -- he has a strong background in both CS and CE and is well equipped to give guidance on this matter. Feel free to pm me too. Lastly, /u/rosewillcode mentioned that CE has IEEE and CS has ACM and NU Hacks, but I just wanted to clarify that there isn't strict segregation; I actually go to all of the above and it's totally cool.
